entries.0014d693965f19ba: Instant bagged noodles (“Chicken Ramen,” “Demae Ichiban,” “Nissin Yakisoba” and the “Nissin Karamyon” series)
entries.074b0724fc471f36: Snack confectionery such as potato chips
entries.0b20214002169352: Chilled foods distributed while kept refrigerated. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, ramen lines performed well, including “Tsukemen no Tatsujin” and “Mazemen no Tatsujin,” which attracted attention for their large portions, and the expanded “Men no Tatsujin” and “Soup no Tatsujin”; cooked noodles for convenience stores also contributed, and revenue increased. Although cost increases, including a higher cost of sales ratio, occurred, higher revenue led to higher profit. Nissin Shokuhin Chiruudo Co., Ltd. is in charge; it was established as a company through an incorporation-type demerger during the transition to a holding company structure in October 2008.
entries.1824d9fac1d7b432: This is a business segment not included in the reportable segments; the company explains that it includes the Domestic Other Business, as well as the Europe Region, Asia Region and New Business. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥59,118 million (up 4.4% year on year), and segment profit (operating profit basis) was ¥7,574 million (down 37.3%). This segment also includes profit or loss of equity-method affiliates; investment gains under the equity method for the fiscal year ended March 2026, amounting to ¥12,949 million, are all recorded in this segment. The 980 employees of the filing company, NISSIN FOODS HOLDINGS CO.,LTD., are also all included in this segment. The number of employees is 2,935 (in addition, an average of 2,553 temporary employees during the year).
entries.21c914c0603e8280: Instant noodles in cups. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, the “Cup Noodles” series performed steadily, and in particular the “Cup Noodles BIG” series, renewed in September 2025, contributed to sales. The starting point was the launch of “Cup Noodles” in September 1971; in October of the same year, the Kanto Plant was completed in Toride, Ibaraki Prefecture, as a production plant. The company states that in the instant noodle industry, relative affordability and convenience have been valued, and demand has grown globally, centered on value-added cup noodles, bringing total world demand to a record high.
entries.285fb7c29bc43375: Instant bagged noodles. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, sales of the main brands “Chicken Ramen,” “Demae Ichiban” and “Nissin Yakisoba” were steady, and the new brand “Nissin Karamyon” series, launched in March 2026, contributed to sales. The starting point of the group as a whole was the development of “Chicken Ramen,” an instant bagged noodle made by the instant oil-heat drying method, in August 1958.
entries.2b0dc16b3d8f53fd: Manufactures and sells cereal foods, confectionery and other products. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, cereal products such as the “Gorogura” series and the “Coconut Sablé” series performed steadily, supported by active marketing measures, and revenue and profit both increased. The company in its present form dates from its equity investment in Sisuko Co., Ltd. in February 1991.
entries.35d38d2347db83d1: Instant noodle business in Europe. Nissin Foods Kft. (Hungary) handles manufacturing and sales, and Nissin Foods GmbH (Germany) handles sales; in Turkey, Nissin Yildiz Gida Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. and NISSIN FOODS TURKEY GIDA ANONIM SIRKETI carry out manufacturing and sales. Premier Foods plc of the United Kingdom (manufacture and sale of processed foods, cooking sauces, confectionery and others; ownership of voting rights 25.2%) and Marven Food Holdings Ltd., the holding company of a group engaged in instant noodle business in Russia (33.5%), are equity-method affiliates.
entries.379f04d095911bfe: Consumers in mainland China, Hong Kong and Taiwan
entries.4e31c81bdf0b54e3: A company that makes instant noodles such as "Chikin Ramen" and "Cup Noodles" in Japan and overseas, and also handles chilled and frozen foods and confectionery.
entries.53276cff8e72d242: Food wholesalers such as Mitsubishi Shokuhin Co., Ltd.
entries.5528c1450842d560: Manufactures and sells rice crackers and snack confectionery (ownership of voting rights: 92.1%). In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue was roughly at the prior-year level, supported by price revisions and specification changes, while profit declined due to cost increases such as higher rice prices. The company took an equity stake in it in February 2014.
entries.57438e2740fc6073: Chinese version of Cup Noodle “Hewei Dao” brand group
entries.5bcb16c21a089e6c: This segment is where Myojo Foods Co., Ltd. mainly manufactures and sells instant bagged noodles and cup noodles. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥48,302 million (up 6.5% year on year); although it was the smallest of the seven segments, its growth rate was the largest, and segment profit (operating profit basis) was ¥3,443 million (up 9.9%), with both revenue and profit increasing. The company states that its marketing strategy for brothless noodles, aimed at a prolonged hot season, was successful, and that its value proposition in the Staple Noodles Series, pursuing noodle quality and showing that bagged noodles can serve as a staple food, led to strong sales. In cup noodles, the “Myojo Ippeichan Yomise no Yakisoba” series and “Myojo Bubuka Abura Soba” contributed to sales, and in bagged noodles, the “Myojo Charumera” series contributed to sales. It is a company in which capital was taken up in December 2006, supported by Uni Star Co., Ltd. (soups) and Higashi Nippon Myojo Co., Ltd. (instant noodles). The company's group has two instant noodle operating companies, Nissin Foods Co., Ltd. and Myojo Foods Co., Ltd., which are listed as separate reportable segments. The number of employees is 614 (in addition, an average of 364 temporary employees during the year).
entries.7a23e3d8e05d598d: Instant noodle business in Asia excluding the China Region. Nissin Foods Asia CO.,LTD. (Thailand) is the regional headquarters company in Asia, and Nissin Foods Vietnam CO.,LTD., India Nissin Foods PRIVATE LTD., Nissin Foods Thailand CO.,LTD., PT NISSIN FOODS INDONESIA, Nissin Foods Singapore PTE.LTD., NISSIN FOODS (CAMBODIA) Co.,LTD. and NISSIN FOODS MALAYSIA SDN BHD are responsible for manufacturing and sales. Thai President Foods Pub.Co.,Ltd. (ownership of voting rights 20.4%) and Nissin-Universal Robina CORP. (Philippines; 49.0%) are equity-method affiliates.
entries.7e51d43c89cc3169: A business in which the company plans to make active and continuous advance investment from the fiscal year ended March 2022 onward, under its medium- to long-term growth strategy. Listing “Promotion of New Businesses” as one of its growth strategy themes, the company uses an indicator called “Core Operating Profit of Existing Businesses,” which separates profit or loss related to this business from operating profit, to measure the substantive growth of existing businesses.
entries.8f48cd0d11e96e81: Consumers in Japan who buy instant noodles through retail
entries.9081f8d9e843d4e8: A category that manufactures and sells chilled products, frozen products and beverage products. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, external revenue was ¥104,167 million (up 2.8% year on year), and segment profit (on an operating profit basis) was ¥7,721 million (down 10.2% year on year). Nissin Shokuhin Chiruudo Co., Ltd., Nissin Shokuhin Reitō Co., Ltd. and Nissin York Co., Ltd. (dairy products and others) are at the core, and Saitama Nissin Shokuhin Co., Ltd., Sagami Fresh Co., Ltd., Shikoku Nissin Shokuhin Co., Ltd., Takamatsu Nissin Shokuhin Co., Ltd., Mie Nissin Shokuhin Co., Ltd. and Nikki Foods Co., Ltd. are in charge of manufacturing. Employees: 953 (plus an annual average of 735 temporary employees).
entries.942d8a1c5669fd32: Frozen foods. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, the “Reitō Nissin Supaō Kissaten” and “Reitō Nissin Chūka” series performed well; frozen ramen for convenience stores also contributed to sales growth, and the effect of price revisions contributed to higher revenue. Although cost increases such as higher raw material prices occurred, higher revenue led to higher profit. Nissin Shokuhin Reitō Co., Ltd. is in charge; it was established as a company through an incorporation-type demerger during the transition to a holding company structure in October 2008. The company states that growth in revenue in the domestic non-instant noodle business was led by this Frozen Business and the Confectionery Business.
entries.9b8b65b03eb9ef37: Cooked rice products in cups. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, new products contributed significantly to sales, and performance was steady. In the product and service information in the securities report, cup rice is classified under “Other Business,” separate from instant noodles.
entries.cb5c527f033958ba: Consumers in the Americas, including the United States, Mexico and Brazil
entries.cd0e647ad4aaf325: Myojo Ippeichan Yomise no Yakisoba series
entries.cf69cc975e557ff9: Beverages centered on dairy products. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, sales of the “Piruku Miracle Care” series declined due to the peak-out of the sleep boom, and sales to convenience stores were sluggish; the contribution from the autumn launches of “Piruku Immunity Style” and “Piruku Aging Life” and the renewal of “Tokachi Nomu Yogurt” was limited, resulting in lower revenue. Higher depreciation expenses from the expansion of the Kansai Plant and higher advertising expenses led to lower profit. Nissin York Co., Ltd. is in charge.
entries.d03844113e763673: Manufactures and sells snack confectionery such as potato chips. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue increased due to the renewal of “Pure Potato,” the strong performance of corn-based brands and price revisions for major potato brands; however, profit declined due to lower yields caused by the poor harvest of Hokkaido-grown potatoes and the effects of high summer temperatures, which led to lower volume, a lower yield rate from quality deterioration, and higher material costs. The company holds 45.12% of the voting rights in it; although it does not hold a majority, it judged that a de facto controlling relationship exists, taking into account the dispersion of voting rights and past voting patterns at shareholders’ meetings, and consolidates it. It files its own securities report, and its 784 employees are the second-largest number in the group after Nissin Foods Co., Ltd. The goodwill and intangible assets recorded in the company’s consolidated statement of financial position are mainly goodwill (carrying amount ¥4,447 million) and trademark rights (carrying amount ¥2,920 million), recognized mainly from its acquisition in fiscal 2020. Overseas, it also has Koikeya Vietnam Co., Ltd., KOIKEYA (THAILAND) Co., Ltd., Taiwan Koikeya Co., Ltd., KOIKEYA AMERICA INC. and Nissin Koikeya (China and Hong Kong) Co., Ltd.
entries.da71b2e5acc93863: A category that manufactures and sells confectionery products. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, external revenue was ¥95,942 million (up 3.8% year on year), and segment profit (on an operating profit basis) was ¥5,277 million (down 2.1% year on year), with revenue up and profit down. Koikeya Co., Ltd., Nissin Cisco Co., Ltd., Bonchi Co., Ltd. and Seria Roiru Co., Ltd. are in charge. Employees: 1,985 (plus an annual average of 1,480 temporary employees).
entries.dd849dc896f7b105: Cup noodles (the “Cup Noodles” series and the “Cup Noodles BIG” series)
entries.f0fe900817d40741: This segment covers domestic business other than instant noodles, chilled foods, beverages and confectionery. Included are Nissin Enterprise Co., Ltd. (warehousing), Circle Liners Co., Ltd. (transport and warehousing), Nissin Foods Direct Marketing Co., Ltd. (planning, development and sale of food, health food and cosmetics), Nissin Foods Asset Management Co., Ltd. (real estate leasing and management), Nissin Netcom Co., Ltd. (real estate management), and Uji Kaihatsu Kogyo Co., Ltd. (golf course operation). In its business description, the securities report states that, centered on the manufacture and sale of instant foods, “we are working to expand into peripheral businesses such as other food businesses and logistics.”
entries.f2e9214ecd40bbaa: Manufactures and sells ice cream and other products (Asakura, Fukuoka Prefecture; ownership of voting rights 68.0%). The company states that it made the aforementioned company a consolidated subsidiary on February 27, 2026.
entries.f2f8f93200a99e49: This segment manufactures and sells mainly instant bagged noodles and cup noodles in mainland China, Hong Kong, Taiwan and other areas. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥74,945 million (up 2.0% year on year), and segment profit (operating profit basis) was ¥8,958 million (up 51.7%), the largest profit growth among the seven segments. The company cites the following: in mainland China, the revitalization of existing sales networks and expansion of sales channels into inland areas led to sales growth, mainly for the Chinese version of Cup Noodle “Hewei Dao” brand group and the bagged noodle brand “Demae Ichiban”; in Hong Kong, instant noodle consumption remained firm, centered on higher-priced new products, and catering sales grew due to an increase in inbound tourists; and, as reasons for the profit increase, in addition to higher revenue, the effect of impairment losses on fixed assets and others recorded in the previous fiscal year. The company states that it is pursuing expansion of sales areas, expansion of sales of higher-priced bagged noodles, multi-category expansion into frozen foods and confectionery, and strengthening of its wholesale business. At its core is Nissin Foods Company Limited, established in Tai Po, Hong Kong, in October 1984 (ownership of voting rights 72.1%; regional management company for China). It is listed on the Main Board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, and the company recognizes significant non-controlling interests (ownership interest 27.95%). Its group's revenue is ¥78,144 million, and profit for the year is ¥6,783 million. Guangdong Shunde Nissin Foods Co., Ltd., Fujian Nissin Foods Co., Ltd., Zhuhai Jinhai'an Yongnan Food Co., Ltd., Zhejiang Nissin Foods Co., Ltd. and others are responsible for manufacturing. The number of employees is 3,764 (in addition, an average of 354 temporary employees during the year).
entries.f8cc36c2bfd573a0: “Piruku” series (“Piruku Miracle Care,” “Piruku Immunity Style,” “Piruku Aging Life”)
